comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh2026–2027 adopted regulation Article1.8 and AppendixII pp40–41,including the original embedded curriculum figure,confirm150requiredEC plus30EC minor. Sixdesign modules60EC,science/skills30,technology25,foundations20,society15. BEP=IOP1+IOP2+TE5+WV6=30EC already counted; no additional thesis. Minor semester5 andfinalBEP semester6 preserve theordinarypathway. Article1.24 advises semesterprogression without imposing a blanket passed-previous-module rule. Personal-development reflections are non-credit requirements feeding WV6. External regulations andprogramme evidence establish design across building/urban/landscape scales as the organising educational activity. Old retrieval histories andspeculative DigiPedia navigation-based computational claims are not retained as current academic proof.

programmes.label: Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: Delft organises this degree around designing buildings, urban ensembles and landscapes, integrating architectural composition with structures, building physics, representation and repeated studio projects. UCR can combine environmental systems, GIS, nature-based interventions, energy and materials with product-design methods, but those courses do not form a sustained architectural and urban-design education.
exception.curriculumContext: The complete 180-EC Delft curriculum is retained: 150 EC of required modules and a 30-EC minor. The final integrated design project is included within those required credits.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: A complete 24-course candidate was tested with Spatial Planning, Energy & Sustainability and Consumer Product Design, alongside nature-based infrastructure, geospatial research, life-cycle analysis and renewable systems. It passes scheduling rules, but its central activities remain environmental analysis, product development and resource systems rather than architectural and urban composition.

candidateAssessment.concept: Environmental systems and spatial design methods
candidateAssessment.assessment: Mechanically feasible strengthened candidate tested. Relevant spatial,material,energy anddesign skills do not establish the programme’s defining integration of built form,structures andarchitectural/urban design practice.

Social theory,economics andgovernance add stakeholder andpublic-decision perspectives,but do not supply a substantive design-led built-environment curriculum. No accepted second alternative follows a rejected closest response.
Renaissance architectural history andmaterial-culture study provide real historical content,but do not form a curriculum inbuilding transformation oradaptive-reuse design.

audience.programmeDescription: Delft’s bachelor develops architectural, urban and landscape design through repeated projects, supported by building technology, design history, social questions, research and representation. A minor and an integrated final design project complete the degree.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers relevant study in sustainability, spatial analysis, energy, materials, nature-based infrastructure and product design. These can support related environmental questions, but they do not provide a sustained programme in architectural and urban design, structures and building physics. A full UCR comparison is therefore not offered.

curriculum.limitation: The 30-EC minor remains open, subject to approval. The final project comprises two integrated design modules, a technology module and a design-reflection module; their credits are already included in the 180-EC total.
